learningObjective: Trace how blank and token transitions consume different axes of the RNN-T lattice, and explain why many monotonic paths can emit the same transcript.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can align acoustic time, emitted-label position, two transition types, and two complete paths on one fixed lattice. The geometry is the lesson: horizontal blank edges advance time, while vertical token edges advance output without consuming another frame.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout does not preserve a regular T-by-U coordinate system or make axis consumption visually exact.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: fixed coordinates keep each node at a precise (t, u) state and permit directly labelled solid and dashed example paths.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table can name lattice states, but connected transitions and alternate monotonic paths would be harder to trace across cell boundaries.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: path stepping would add controls and runtime state without teaching more than two static, fully labelled example alignments.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: Graves's paper and the local deck include related lattice figures, but no permissive figure-reuse license was established. The shipped lattice, paths, labels, wording, and proportions are independently authored.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose asks readers to mentally coordinate two asynchronous axes and a sum over paths. A small lattice makes the blank-versus-token invariant and alignment marginalization directly inspectable.

pages.insight: The preceding CTC slide introduces blank-labelled alignments and dynamic-programming summation, establishing the one-dimensional mechanism that RNN-T extends.

The dedicated RNN-T slide names the transcription, prediction, and joint networks; describes all T-by-U joint combinations; and states that horizontal blank transitions consume frames while vertical non-blank transitions consume labels.
The following slide begins a new topic and contains no additional RNN-T architecture, alignment, or decoding material.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-4 text-indexed the complete 214-page local deck for RNN-T, transducer, CTC, speech recognition, blank, and forward-backward references, then inspected the exact page 125-127 neighborhood. Page 126 is the sole dedicated RNN-T slide. Its text explicitly refers to Graves's lattice figure, but the deck gives no asset-level reuse license, so no deck image, wording, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: Sequence Transduction with Recurrent Neural Networks
sources.usage: Used as the primary source for the transcription, prediction, and joint-network factorization; the output lattice; blank and non-blank transitions; and forward-backward summation over alignments.
sources.license: The arXiv record provides public access but does not establish a permissive license for reusing the paper's figures. No figure, prose, example path, or paper-specific layout is copied or adapted.

sources.title: Streaming End-to-End Speech Recognition for Mobile Devices
sources.usage: Used as a primary production reference to verify the use of RNN-T for streaming, on-device speech recognition and the modern encoder, prediction-network, and joint-network formulation.
sources.license: No paper figure, table, prose, or empirical result is reused. The source is consulted only for technical claims, and public arXiv access is not treated as figure-reuse permission.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only model is the asynchronous T-by-U lattice: a blank consumes acoustic time without emitting a label, while a token emits a label without advancing acoustic time. The original schematic uses a synthetic two-token target and no paper data. Both example paths are monotonic and contain exactly three blank transitions and two token transitions.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, inspected the full deck index and exact RNN-T slide neighborhood, and checked the foundational and production RNN-T papers before selecting an original two-path lattice.

implementation.accessibility: Each SVG panel has a linked title and complete description. Axes, transition labels, node coordinates, and both path sequences are written explicitly; blank transitions use horizontal arrows and the blank symbol, while token transitions use vertical arrows and token text, so color is redundant. The established two-panel primitive stacks below 640 pixels, allowing each compact 300-pixel viewBox to use the full article width at 390 CSS pixels; theme variables support dark mode, and shared print rules provide a light high-contrast rendering.
